memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If, when the priest examines it, the mould has faded after the article has been washed, he is to tear the spoiled part out of the fabric, the leather, or the woven or knitted material. But if it reappears in the fabric, in the woven or knitted material, or in the leather article, it is spreading, and whatever has the mould must be burned with fire." - Lev 13:56-57 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A middle path at last. If the mould had faded, the priest did not burn the whole garment. He tore out the affected part and kept the rest.

There is real grace in that. God does not destroy everything because something has gone wrong in a corner of it. He is a God who preserves what can be preserved.

That matters for how we think about ourselves. When we discover something ugly in our hearts — a prejudice we did not know we held, a selfishness exposed by pressure — we can swing towards a kind of despair, concluding that everything about us is rotten and nothing is worth keeping. God does not work that way. He is precise. He removes what must go and preserves what He has made.

But note the honesty of the second half. If it comes back, the garment is burned. God's patience is not indefinite indulgence, and repeated warnings unheeded eventually reach a conclusion.

Jesus spoke of the Father as a gardener who prunes the fruitful branch so it will be even more fruitful (John 15:2). Pruning hurts, and it looks like loss. But the gardener's aim is never destruction. It is a better harvest from a plant he has every intention of keeping.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend towards despair when God exposes something in you?
2. What might God be pruning in your life right now?
3. Is there a warning you have received more than once and not yet acted on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are precise in Your dealing with me — removing what must go without discarding me. Give me a soft heart to Your pruning and Your warnings. Amen.
